2607.27384.title: Same Facts, Different Diagnosis: Measuring and Mitigating Narrative Anchoring in Clinical Language Models
2607.27384.paper_summary: Large language models used for clinical diagnostic reasoning are sensitive to sociolinguistic register, not just clinical content. We term this failure mode Narrative Anchoring: identical clinical facts expressed in different registers cause diagnostic outputs to diverge. Unlike prior demographic-bias work, which manipulates explicit identity tokens such as race or income, our benchmark isolates register as the sole channel of variation, with no demographic marker present in any form. We construct a dataset of 1,000 USMLE clinical vignettes, each rewritten into three sociolinguistically distinct personas under an independently audited fact-preservation guarantee, verified by a separate model that never sees the generation prompt. Across seven language models spanning three architecture families and scales, Narrative Anchoring is statistically significant under direct prompting in every model tested, with a Narrative Anchoring Gap of 0.064 to 0.151. Chain-of-thought reasoning and explicit debiasing instructions reduce the bias only partially, and their apparent gains are frequently confounded by accuracy collapse. We introduce NarrativeShield, a three-agent pipeline that structurally extracts and verifies clinical facts before diagnostic reasoning begins, reducing the Narrative Anchoring Gap to near-zero ($-0.004$ to $0.037$) and achieving the lowest rate of severely unstable decisions (DSS $<$ 0.8) of any method across all models, at a modest and mechanistically expected accuracy cost for most models. A stress test using a non-instruction-tuned base model shows that executing a debiasing intervention at all is gated by zero-shot instruction-following ability, not prompt content alone. We release our dataset, human-validated for fact preservation, as a standalone resource for studying register-based clinical bias.
2607.27384.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型在臨床診斷推理中對社會語言註冊敏感，而不僅僅是臨床內容。我們將這種失效模式稱為敘事錨定：以不同註冊表達的相同臨床事實會導致診斷結果的分歧。與之前操縱明確身份標記（如種族或收入）的群體偏見研究不同，我們的基準將註冊作為唯一的變異通道，任何形式都不包含人口標記。我們構建了一個包含1,000個USMLE臨床小插曲的數據集，每個小插曲都在獨立審核的事實保留保證下，重寫成三個社會語言上不同的人物，並由一個從未看到生成提示的獨立模型進行驗證。在涵蓋三個架構系列和規模的七個語言模型中，敘事錨定在每個測試模型中都在直接提示下具有統計顯著性，敘事錨定差距為0.064到0.151。思維鏈推理和明確的去偏見指令僅部分減少了偏見，且其顯著增益常常因準確性崩潰而受到干擾。我們引入了NarrativeShield，一個三代理的管道，在診斷推理開始之前結構性地提取和驗證臨床事實，將敘事錨定差距降低至接近零（$-0.004$到$0.037$），並在所有模型中實現了任何方法中最低的嚴重不穩定決策率（DSS $<$ 0.8），對於大多數模型而言，其準確性成本適中且在機械上是預期的。使用未經指令調整的基礎模型進行的壓力測試顯示，執行去偏見干預的能力受到零樣本指令跟隨能力的限制，而不僅僅是提示內容。我們發布了經人類驗證的事實保留數據集，作為研究基於註冊的臨床偏見的獨立資源。
